summary: Deferred access revocation for extended leave: conditional device recovery & sudo signal
description:
Issue summary:
An engineer was put on an approved medical leave (FMLA-equivalent) with temporary reduced access for 90 days. HR followed the deferred-revocation process that preserves emergency sudo for the manager and a limited set of service accounts. We need clarification and an operational plan for: (1) signaling emergency sudo revocation if HR later decides to enforce immediate revocation, (2) collecting the engineer's company laptop after 30 days if leave is extended beyond the original window, and (3) wiping encrypted disks remotely vs. in-person collection.

Impact:
- Potential risk if emergency sudo remains active longer than intended (affects privilege hygiene).
- Unclear collection window creates logistics risk for device recovery and asset accounting.
- Legal/HR constraints require we avoid premature account termination.

Environment:
- Internal offboarding/leave workflows; affected identity is in Okta and Azure AD; device is corporate MacBook (FileVault enabled) enrolled in Intune/MDM.
- Region: us-west (employee based in US).

Steps / requested action:
1) Confirm the signal mechanism for immediate emergency sudo revocation (who can trigger, what playbook/automation exists, expected propagation time).
2) Create a short plan for conditional device recovery at 30/60/90 days with owner contact steps, courier options, and remote wipe policy decision matrix tied to HR approvals.
3) Recommend a safe remote wipe/run-wipe fallback that preserves forensics if needed and complies with HR/legal constraints.
4) If automation is required (e.g., a webhook from HR system to IAM), list required scopes and an outline PR for engineering.

Attachments / references:
- HR leave approval case: HR-57321 (internal HR tracker link)
- Current offboarding playbook: https://confluence.redwood/HR/OffboardingPlaybook
- MDM device record: device-id-REDACTED
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (reporter): Opening ticket after HR asked for an operational plan; flagged that legal requires no account termination without sign-off.
2026-03-11 - Markus Chen (assignee): Noted existing playbook has a 'deferred-revoke' section but no automation; requesting MDM team contact and device courier costs estimate.

2026-03-12 - Jenna Morales (HR partner): Confirmed HR can authorize immediate revocation but asked for a minimal-impact checklist that preserves pay/benefits timelines. HR prefers courier-first for devices when possible.

2026-03-12 - SRE oncall (Marco Li): Asked whether remote wipe should be single-step or two-step (lock then wipe) to preserve forensic image if required; recommended two-step with quarantine label in MDM.
investigation_notes: Reviewed playbook: deferred-revoke section is ambiguous about 'emergency toggle' and references a Slack-only signal in #security with no audit webhook.
Checked Okta access history: engineer's emergency sudo was granted to manager via group 'emergency-sudo-rotating' created at onboarding. No automatic removal scheduled.

MDM (Intune) supports remote lock and full wipe APIs; enrollment indicates FileVault enabled which allows remote wipe without key escrow access. Forensics team advises image capture before wipe if HR/legal suspects wrongdoing.

Possible automation: HR could post to internal webhook that calls a small service to remove the manager from 'emergency-sudo-rotating' and trigger a device collection workflow. Scope will require Okta SCIM removal rights and MDM API token with device-read and wipe permissions.
resolution: (Draft) Agreed path: 1) Add an 'Emergency Revoke' checkbox in HR case UI that triggers an authenticated webhook to the 'offboard-orchestrator' service. That service will remove the manager from the emergency-sudo group in Okta (SCIM call) and post an audit entry to the security log. 2) Device recovery: default courier pickup scheduled at day 30 if leave extends; if courier not possible, team will attempt remote lock at day 30 and remote wipe at day 45 after forensic hold evaluation. 3) Engineering to create a small PR (offboard-orchestrator) implementing SCIM remove + MDM lock endpoint. 4) Legal/HR to sign off on the forensic hold timeline. Next steps: assign PR to infra team, draft HR UI change, and schedule a 30-minute alignment call with Security, HR, and MDM owners.
